title: Components of injective towers are acyclic
statement:
Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and schemes $T,S$, and put $R_{T,r}=\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^r$ and $R_{S,r}=\mathcal O_{E,S}/\ell^r$ as in [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], with the canonical identification $g^{-1}R_{S,r}\simeq R_{T,r}$ for every morphism $g:T\to S$. Use the small pro-etale sites with the size convention of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $I_\bullet$ be an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions] of $\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E)$. Then for every $r\geq1$, the component $I_r$ is a direct summand of a finite product of sheaves $J_n$ ($1\leq n\leq r$), each an injective $R_{T,n}$-module viewed as an $R_{T,r}$-module by restriction along $R_{T,r}\to R_{T,n}$. In particular $I_r$ is acyclic for sections over every object of $T_{\mathrm{proet}},$ hence $g_*$-acyclic [def-sp-acyclic] for every morphism $g:T\to S$, where $g_*$ is the ordinary module direct image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] for the coefficient identification $g^{-1}R_{S,r}\simeq R_{T,r}$.

Here $g_{*,\bullet}$ denotes the additive left exact functor on coefficient towers obtained by applying these ordinary direct images levelwise, with the transitions induced by the original transitions; $Rg_{*,\bullet}$ denotes its total right derived functor on $D^+$ [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. Evaluation and $C_n$ have the meaning of [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Consequently, for $C_\bullet\in D^+(\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E))$ with a bounded below injective resolution $C_\bullet\to I_\bullet^\cdot$, the complex $g_*I_n^\cdot$ represents $Rg_{*,\mathcal O_E/\ell^n}C_n$, and there is a natural isomorphism
$$(Rg_{*,\bullet}C_\bullet)_n\simeq Rg_{*,\mathcal O_E/\ell^n}C_n.$$

proof.text: Work in the common larger universe and small site models specified by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For either scheme and each coefficient ring sheaf, [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] gives a Grothendieck abelian module category, hence enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. The tower categories are Grothendieck abelian by [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian], so the same enough-injectives theorem applies to them. Thus all module and tower injective resolutions used below exist in the stated categories.

source.place: Tag 079H, theorem-injective-embedding-grothendieck; blueprint proof, ambient coefficient categories

proof.text: Apply [det-sp-tower-evaluation-adjoint] to obtain a monomorphism $a:I_\bullet\hookrightarrow P_\bullet=\prod_{n\geq1}r_nJ_n$, with $J_n$ injective over $R_n$. By [def-sp-injective-resolutions], the identity of $I_\bullet$ extends across $a$, giving $b:P_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ with $ba=1$. Products of the systems in [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers] are levelwise: the projections and a map into the product are defined componentwise, and compatibility with transitions is checked after each projection. Since $(r_nJ_n)_r=0$ for $n>r$ and equals the restriction of $J_n$ for $n\leq r$, evaluation of $ba=1$ exhibits $I_r$ as a retract of the finite product $\prod_{n\leq r}\operatorname{Res}_{R_r\to R_n}J_n$. T4 formalization uses the ordinary left adjoint supplied by [lem-pur-system-level-left-extension]: system evaluation is a right adjoint and therefore preserves the countable product in the embedding. This replaces the explicit construction of pointwise small limits. The equivalence counit identifies its factors with the recorded strict levels; the lower zero factors are omitted by an explicit finite-product isomorphism. This works also at r=0 in the Lean indexing, where there is one factor.

source.place: First paragraph: embedding, splitting, and finite product at each level

proof.text: Transport the pro-etale site to its AsSmall model in the common coefficient universe, using the induced topology and the explicit module pushforward equivalence. Equivalences preserve injectives and are exact. On that small model apply [lem-sc-injective-module-abelian-acyclic-zariski] to the injective module. [lem-sc-site-cohomology-right-derived-sections] identifies its positive abelian cohomology with positive right derived abelian evaluation. Scalar restriction leaves the abelian sheaf unchanged. The generic exact-composition comparisons compRightDerivedObjIso and rightDerivedCompObjIso identify derived module evaluation after the exact faithful module-to-abelian-group functor with this derived abelian evaluation; faithfulness reflects the resulting zero object. Transport back along the exact module equivalence to obtain section acyclicity on the original pro-etale site. No flatness or preservation of injectives by scalar restriction is used. These are the acyclic-resolution comparisons of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity]. This direct comparison works for the arbitrary induced Grothendieck topology and does not require choosing a precoverage presentation for it.

source.place: Tag 03FD, lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree, second equality and proof of injective-module abelian acyclicity

proof.text: The additive higher right-derived functors preserve finite biproducts, hence their acyclic-object property is closed under binary products and contains zero. The finite-product closure theorem gives section acyclicity of the product of restricted injectives. Apply each positive derived section functor to the evaluated retract. Its section factor embeds into a zero object, hence is zero. This uses [def-sp-left-exact-additive] and the injective/acyclic-resolution properties of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity], without any infinite-product exactness assertion.

source.place: Second paragraph: finite products and direct summands preserve higher-section vanishing; explicit elementary argument

proof.text: Use the dimension-shifting acyclicity criterion rightAcyclic_of_epi_map_g from the existing acyclicity API [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity], with P the property of being acyclic for sections over every pro-etale object. Injectives satisfy P by the generic vanishing of positive right derived functors on injectives. The long exact derived section sequence shows P is closed under cokernels of monomorphisms between P-objects. For a short exact sequence with first term in P, evaluation over every base-changed object is short exact by map_of_rightAcyclic. The section formula of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] therefore makes the direct image of its last map sectionwise surjective. The module-presheaf epimorphism criterion and the faithful full sheaf inclusion yield an epimorphism of module sheaves. The acyclicity criterion proves [def-sp-acyclic] for direct image. This is the dimension-shifting form of the blueprint sheafification-of-cohomology argument, using only left exactness and the section formula of the actual direct image.

source.place: Second paragraph, final sentence; compare Stacks sites-cohomology.tex Tag 072W, lemma-higher-direct-images

proof.text: By exactness of evaluation in [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian], the evaluated injective tower complex is bounded below. Each term is finite-level direct-image acyclic by step 5. Apply [src-right-derived-functor-plus-acyclic-unit] to obtain invertibility of the specified finite-level derived unit. Exact evaluation itself has invertible derived unit by [src-sbc-exact-functor-plus-unit]. For an arbitrary supplied resolution isomorphism, compose the finite-level unit, the image of the exact evaluation unit, and the derived image of the inverse resolution isomorphism. Each factor is invertible; asIso of this precise composite proves the required normalized resolution computation.

source.place: Tag 015E, lemma-leray-acyclicity; Tag 05TH, lemma-injective-acyclic; blueprint proof, final paragraph

proof.text: For the concrete product-site tower pushforward, coefficient naturality follows from the sheafification adjunction, assembled by NatTrans.ofOpSequence and uncurrying. Continuous sheaf pushforward preserves the vertical sheaf condition. Finite limits of module presheaves are pointwise; the vertical sheaf condition is closed under them because limits of sheaves are sheaves. Thus the full-subcategory inclusion preserves finite limits. Pointwise scalar restriction proves that presheaf pushforward preserves them, and reflection by the target full-subcategory inclusion proves that tower pushforward does too. Additivity follows from finite-product preservation. The section normalizations in [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian] identify the two underived evaluation section modules. Their restriction and morphism normalizations show that the identity on sections assembles into a natural linear isomorphism. Sectionwise faithfulness gives its uniqueness. The levelwise tower direct image defined in the statement is additive and left exact: both properties are checked at each level, using the section formula of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and the levelwise kernels of [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Its source has enough injectives by step 1. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] therefore represents $Rg_{*,\bullet}C_\bullet$ by $g_{*,\bullet}I_\bullet^\cdot$. Exact evaluation gives its level-$n$ representative $g_*I_n^\cdot$. Step 6 identifies this complex with $Rg_{*,\mathcal O_E/\ell^n}C_n$, proving the displayed isomorphism. The comparison is the one induced by the underived evaluation identity and the derived units. Their naturality, and the uniqueness clause (3) of the same right-derived-functor node, make it independent of the injective resolution and natural in $C_\bullet$. In Lean, the composite tower-push/evaluation unit is invertible on injective complexes because the tower-push unit is invertible there and exact evaluation has an invertible unit everywhere, by [src-sbc-exact-functor-plus-unit]. For evaluation followed by finite-level push, step 5 and the acyclic composition theorem give the other right derived functor. Transport along the underived homotopy comparison using rightDerivedNatIso. Its unit equation gives the displayed compatibility, and rightDerived_ext gives uniqueness. The right-derived uniqueness argument is proved first as a private lemma for abstract abelian categories and then instantiated, so kernel checking does not repeatedly unfold the concrete tower categories.

source.place: Final paragraph: tower derived direct image, evaluation and the comparison; Stacks derived.tex Tags 05TI and 05TH

proof_origin.place: All three paragraphs, with Stacks 03FD and 015E supplying the cited general tools and elementary finite-product/sheaf-exactness details written out; X8 stage 3 formalization: direct D+ acyclic-unit and exact-unit computations, and uniqueness of the composite right derived functors; no separate K-injectivity argument is needed by these D+ declarations. X8 continuation also proves pointwise finite-limit preservation and the unique identity-on-sections underived evaluation comparison from the published section, restriction and morphism normalizations. The final derived uniqueness proof is factored through a fully proved private generic lemma for efficient kernel checking. T4 closes the last original hole by the existing ordinary left adjunction for system evaluation, the finite-support product isomorphism, module equivalences to the common-universe AsSmall site, the existing abelian cohomology and acyclic-resolution comparisons, and the dimension-shifting direct-image acyclicity criterion. No new unproved result or interface change. T4 also factors the existing coefficient-map naturality, presheaf pushforward finite-limit preservation, and identity-on-sections evaluation comparison through fully proved private generic/component helpers to avoid expensive coefficient-definition unfolding; helper instance attributes are local. The evaluated-product retract is factored through a fully proved private generic helper, and the concrete level-pushforward additive instance is registered locally to avoid repeated typeclass search.
